_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: Wordle was built as a gift for one person.
beats.note: Josh Wardle made it in January 2021 for his partner, Palak Shah.

beats.text: She cut about 12,000 words down to roughly 2,500.
beats.note: Shah kept the commonly known ones so the daily puzzle felt fair.

beats.context: Roughly how many played on 1 November 2021. It passed 300,000 by 2 January 2022.

beats.text: The shareable emoji squares came from friends in New Zealand.
beats.note: Wardle added the format, and results spread across Twitter.

beats.text: He never wanted it to be a full-time job.
beats.note: The game had no adverts, and Wardle has said making money was not the goal.

beats.text: The New York Times bought it in January 2022 for a low seven figure sum.

beats.line: Big apps often start as small gifts.
